lines.li: [us] How long were you on the road?
[them,their:tribal] Many sleeps, and the last of them cold.
[them,their:medieval] A week and more, and the inns got worse the closer I came.
[them,their:spacer] Longer than I'd budgeted for, put it that way.
[them] Long enough to wish for a proper bed.
[us] Well, you made it.
[us] Did you come far?
[them] From {TOWN}, it's barely a walk.
[us] Then we should see more of you.
[them,likesus] You will, if you'll have me.
[them] Maybe so.
[them] We walked through rain the whole last stretch.
[us] Come in under a roof and dry off, at least.
[them,their:tribal] Rain is only the sky washing its face.
[them,their:hightech] My coat's meant to keep this out, and it doesn't.
[them] I'll take you up on that.
[us] You came through all this?
[them,their:tribal] Snow is only water that has gone to sleep.
[them,home:frozen] This is a light dusting where I come from.
[them] Snow to the knees in places, and it isn't letting up.
[us] Then warm yourself before you head back.
[them] Is it always like this out here?
[us] Not always, but often enough.
[them,their:tribal] The sky is angry with someone, and I hope it isn't me.
[them] Then I'll wait it out, if you don't mind.
[them] I nearly walked past your gate in this fog.
[us] It comes in thick here, then lifts all at once.
[them] I'll believe that when I see it.
[us] Hot enough for you?
[them,home:desert] This is nothing, you should feel the sand at home.
[them,home:cold] I'm melting, we never get heat like this at home.
[them] More than enough, thank you.
[us] Find some shade while you're here.
[us] Cold enough for you?
[them,home:frozen] At home we'd call this a mild day.
[them,home:hot] I can't feel my fingers, how do you live like this?
[them] Colder than I'd like, that's for sure.
[us] You get used to it, mostly.
[them] You picked a pretty spot for it, I'll say that.
[us] On days like this, it picks itself.
[them] Everything's coming up green on the way here.
[us] It's the best time of year out here.
[them,their:tribal] The herds are fattening again, and so are we, nearly.
[them,their:medieval] The lambing's done at home, and the plowing's begun.
[them] It's the best time of year anywhere, I'd say.
[us] Long days for traveling, at least.
[them] Long days, short nights, and flies the size of my thumb.
[us] We've got those too.
[us] Harvest time where you are too?
[them,town:short:food] What there is of it, and it isn't much.
[them,their:lowtech,!town:short:food] Everyone who can hold a sickle is in the fields.
[them,!town:short:food] Everyone's busy with it, I barely got away.
[us] Then we're lucky you came.
[them] Not many travel this time of year.
[us] What brought you out, then?
[them,role:trader] Silver, same as always.
[them,role:guest] A warm bed and kind company, I hoped.
[them,their:hightech] A heated room and someone new to talk to.
[them] Something to do besides sit by the fire.
[us] What's the land like around {TOWN}?
[them] {HOMELAND}, mostly, as far as you can see.
[us] Do you like it there?
[them,their:tribal] It feeds us and hides us, so we love it.
[them,home:mountains] I like the mountains, they keep the wind off and the raiders out.
[them] It's home, I don't think about it more than that.
[us] What's it like where you live?
[them] Sand, sun and wind, and water worth more than silver.
[us] I don't think I'd last a week.
[them] You'd be surprised what you can get used to.
[us] Is it cold where you're from?
[them] Cold enough that we count the year in thaws.
[us] And you like it there?
[them,their:tribal] The cold keeps the weak away, and we are not weak.
[them] It's home, and the cold keeps the crowds away.
[them] I can still smell the sea on my coat.
[us] You live by the water?
[them,their:tribal] We fish when the sea allows and pray when it doesn't.
[them] Right by it, the waves are the last thing I hear at night.
[us] Are there woods around {TOWN}?
[them] Trees as far as you can walk in a day, and farther.
[them,their:tribal] The trees remember our names, so the elders say.
[us] It must be quiet.
[them] Quiet, until the wolves start singing.
[them] Your air is so dry, I keep wanting a drink.
[us] Is it wet where you live?
[them] Wet, green and loud, and everything bites.
[us] You make it sound lovely.
[them] It is, once you stop scratching.
[them] It's warmer here than at home, I'll give you that.
[us] Is it cold in {TOWN} now?
[them,their:lowtech] Cold enough that we sleep in our boots.
[them] Cold enough that I'm in no hurry to go back.
[them] It's cooler here than at home, it's a mercy.
[us] Is {TOWN} that hot just now?
[them] Hot enough to cook on the stones.
[us] Why do you travel, {OUTSIDER}?
[them,role:trader] Silver, mostly, and I like the road.
[them,role:guest] For the company, and a change of walls.
[them,their:tribal] The young must walk far before they sit by the fire.
[them] Someone has to see the world, it might as well be me.
[us] I'd like to see more of it myself.
[them] Then come and see {TOWN} one day.
[them] Then go, before you're too settled to.
